entry.title: How did Africa become a symbol of freedom?

media:group.media:title: How did Africa become a symbol of freedom?
media:group.media:description:
How did Africa’s image become a symbol of freedom, solidarity and unity?
As part of #BlackHistoryMonth, Karrington Harp shares her key takeaways from Oxford’s Black History Month Lecture 2026, The Iconicity of Africa, delivered by Professor Adom Getachew.
The lecture explored the history and enduring influence of Pan-Africanism and was organised by Oxford’s BME Staff Network in partnership with Nuffield College and the University's Equality and Diversity Unit.

entry.title: Oxford researcher reveals the psychology behind The Traitors with a former Faithful

media:group.media:title: Oxford researcher reveals the psychology behind The Traitors with a former Faithful
media:group.media:description:
'The biggest mistake is not making bad judgements; it’s believing them to be correct.'
As we head towards the final of The Celebrity Traitors, DPhil student Isaac Winterburn from Oxford's Department of Experimental Psychology explores the game's psychology, from confirmation bias to why we're not as good at spotting liars as we think.
Joining him is psychologist and former Faithful Dr Ellie Buckley, who shares her insights from inside the castle.
With thanks to Dr Ellie Buckley and the Oxford Psychology Society for their contributions to this video.
#TheTraitors #Psychology #OxfordUniversity

entry.title: 'One in four of us will have a stroke in our lifetime.'

media:group.media:title: 'One in four of us will have a stroke in our lifetime.'
media:group.media:description:
- 'High blood pressure affects one in three adults and is the most important risk factor for stroke.' - 'Acting fast can make all the difference.'
Every five minutes, someone in the UK has a stroke. But how much do you really know about the risks?
For #WorldStrokeDay, researchers from Oxford’s Nuffield Department of Clinical Neurosciences share what they wish more people knew about stroke.

media:group.media:title: The Lincoln College Imp
media:group.media:description:
Discover the curious story of the Lincoln College Imp, a small, mischievous figure hidden within the college.
Once associated with the devil himself, the Lincoln Imp has had something of a reputation makeover over the centuries and is now seen as a much-loved symbol of the College.
But how did he get here? And where is the original Imp now?
#OxfordUniversity #Oxford #LincolnCollege #OxfordHistory
